The design is fixed and all tests pass.

I found two bugs in `rtl/hamming_secded.v`:
1. The `flip` mask for syndromes 9 (data bit d4) and 10 (data bit d5) were swapped, so correcting those positions flipped the wrong bit.
2. `correctable`/`single_err`/`double_err`/`data` logic only checked `parity`, not whether `syn` was actually in the correctable range (1..12). This caused two issues: syndromes 13-15 (spec rule 4, uncorrectable) were misreported as single-bit corrections, and double-bit errors whose syndrome happened to match a valid single-bit position (e.g. syn=3) incorrectly flipped a data bit instead of leaving `data` unmodified as required by rule 5.

I fixed both by correcting the flip mask table and gating `correctable` on `syn <= 12`, with `data` only XORed with `flip` when correctable. Verified against `tb/tb_visible.v` (TEST PASSED) plus additional manual checks for the d4/d5 swap and the double-error/syn-collision case.
